title: FancyZones app-running-as-administrator prompt doesn't honor the don't show again option

status.label: Make elevated-warning dismissal persistent
status.detail: The elevated-app toast uses a 30-day dismissal timestamp; the existing warning setting provides a visible, reversible way to honor "Don't show again."

next_action.label: Approve the setting-backed dismissal
next_action.reason: Persistently disabling the existing elevated-app warning setting matches the button label and leaves the separate preview-toast timeout unchanged.

judgment.rationale: The latest investigation identifies the precise mismatch: the elevated-app warning stores a timestamp that is honored for only 30 days. Current code separately reads the existing enable_warnings_elevated_apps setting, so making the button persistently disable that visible setting is a concrete and reversible fix; the preview-modules toast can retain its current 30-day behavior.
evidence: The 2022 report says the warning returns after a restart or new Windows flight; later users report repeated warnings.
The 2026-10-11 issue comment reproduces the return by backdating the elevated-warning registry timestamp by 45 days and identifies ElevatedDisableIntervalInDays = 30.
Current upstream at 2d28a562bfb5f8a76c4a43bbd8c3939f827bb368 calls is_toast_disabled(ElevatedDontShowAgainRegistryPath, ElevatedDisableIntervalInDays) for the elevated-app warning.
Current NotificationUtil::ReadSettings loads enable_warnings_elevated_apps, providing an existing user-visible and reversible setting; the preview toast uses a separate registry path and interval.
judgment.recommended_action: Change the elevated-warning button activation to persistently disable the existing enable_warnings_elevated_apps setting; keep the preview-modules toast on its existing 30-day suppression behavior and verify that users can re-enable the warning in Settings.

fix_assessment.rationale: The 30-day timestamp is directly confirmed in current code and reproduces the reported recurrence. Reusing the existing setting makes the dismissal durable and visible without changing the separate preview-toast policy.

proposed_fixes.title: Persistently disable the elevated-app warning when dismissed
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The elevated-app warning uses the generic timestamp-based toast suppression with a 30-day interval. After that interval the warning is eligible again, despite the button promising not to show it again. The existing enable_warnings_elevated_apps setting is a user-visible and reversible control.
plan: Update the elevated-warning activation path to persistently set enable_warnings_elevated_apps to false when the user selects "Don't show again."
Keep the preview-modules toast on its own 30-day timestamp-based suppression path; do not make the shared helper permanent for all toasts.
Add coverage for dismissal across module/process restart and settings updates, and verify that turning the existing warning setting back on restores the warning.
verification: After dismissing the elevated-app warning, restarting FancyZones or Always On Top does not show it again.
The preview-modules toast still uses its existing 30-day dismissal interval.
Re-enabling the elevated-app warning in Settings allows the warning to appear again when its trigger occurs.

confidence.rationale: The 30-day expiry is explicit in the current helper and is the direct cause of the reported recurrence; the existing setting is already read by the warning utility and is reversible.

issue_context.summary: The FancyZones and Always On Top elevated-app warning returns after the user selects "Don't show again."
known_information: The original report used PowerToys 0.58.0 and observed the warning after restarting or starting a new Windows session.
The latest investigation reports that the elevated-warning dismissal is stored as a timestamp and expires after 30 days; backdating it by 45 days reproduces the warning.
Current upstream uses a 30-day interval for the elevated-app warning and separately loads the enable_warnings_elevated_apps setting.
The preview-modules toast has a separate registry path and a separate 30-day interval.
inferences: A permanent, reversible setting change is more consistent with the "Don't show again" button than an expiring timestamp.
The preview-modules toast should retain its existing temporary suppression behavior because it uses a distinct notification path.
issue_context.analysis: The 30-day suppression explains why the button appears to work initially but the warning later returns. The existing warning setting offers a visible way to reverse the choice, unlike a hidden permanent registry dismissal. Keep the change limited to the elevated-app warning so the preview-toast policy does not change.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue body and comments, including the 2026-10-11 reproduction and proposed alternatives.
Inspected current upstream NotificationUtil.cpp and dont_show_again.h: the elevated warning uses the 30-day timestamp helper, while NotificationUtil::ReadSettings reads the existing warning setting.
